BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Status:** Privileged and confidential. Internal buyer advice.

## 1. Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every protected position. Taken together, the changes would:

- reduce the Seller's real exposure well below our baseline;
- pull Title and fraud into the capped general regime;
- let the Seller treat the whole data room as disclosed; and
- leave three Completion-critical items (Bluefen, Riverlark and the DD-005 bonuses) unresolved, while describing them as "addressed".

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several statements in its covering Update. That helps us in the mark-up.

## 2. The "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing

The preamble says these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and "are not intended to be re-opened". We should not accept or rely on that.

- **No authority on our side.** The playbook records that Amelia Frost has given no written authority for the 20% cap fallback or the 18-month fallback. Nothing in our instructions shows any principal-level agreement on these terms. Unless Amelia confirms otherwise in writing, treat every position as open.
- **"Market" claims are assertions, not agreed terms.** The 10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are the Seller's characterisation. They do not bind us.
- **Recommended action:** confirm internally with Amelia Frost that nothing was agreed. Then say in the cover note to our mark-up that no position is accepted as final.

## 3. Issue-by-issue departures

### A. Liability architecture

| # | Clause | Seller position | Playbook | Issue / pushback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.1 Cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | 20% is our conditional fallback and needs prior written Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft. None has been given. **Reinstate 25% / AUD 6.0m.** Do not signal that a fallback exists. |
| 2 | 12.2 De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Five times our position. Many genuine SaaS warranty claims (individual contracts, small tax items) would be screened out. **Reinstate AUD 5,000.** |
| 3 | 12.2 Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, tipping basket (first dollar) | This is two problems: a basket five times larger, and a deductible structure. Together they mean the first AUD 250k of losses is never recoverable. **Reinstate AUD 50,000 tipping.** |
| 4 | 12.3 General claims period | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost approval. None given. It would also likely cover only one full audit cycle after Completion. **Reinstate 24 months.** |
| 5 | 12.3 / 13 "limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated" | Default rule extending general limitations everywhere | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **This is a key structural trap.** It flips the default so that every specific indemnity, covenant, payment obligation, leakage or price-adjustment claim becomes capped, basketed and time-barred unless carved out word-for-word. **Delete it.** Replace it with an express statement that general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. |
| 6 | Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | "Administrative simplicity" does not justify capping title at 20% on a 100% share purchase. A title failure means we did not get what we paid for. **Reject. Reinstate the separate Fundamental regime.** |
| 7 | 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" | No fraud carve-out | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable | **Most serious drafting point.** "Claims of any nature" on its face captures fraud claims. That cannot be waived on our side. Under NSW law, attempts to exclude liability for one's own fraud are generally ineffective. Even so, we must not sign wording that purports to do so, and we want the carve-out to cover wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct as well. **Insert a standalone, overriding carve-out.** Non-reliance must also not exclude claims for misleading or deceptive conduct based on fraud, to the extent enforceable. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**8. General disclosure (DL 1.1 and 1.2)**

The Seller discloses:

- every fact "contained *or referred to*" in the whole data room, which can reach documents outside the data room;
- the Accounts;
- the statutory registers; and
- "publicly searchable corporate records".

This is exactly the whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure our playbook rejects.

Pushback:
- Only specific disclosures fairly made in the letter count, meaning enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its effect.
- **Delete 1.1 and 1.2.**
- Disclosure should never qualify Title or Capacity warranties, fraud, or any specific indemnity.

The data room is fixed "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026", which is now six weeks old. If any data-room reference survives, it must be a fixed, indexed and agreed copy. Any update between signing and Completion must not cure a breach or reduce our remedies. At most, a new matter could give us a walk-away right.

**9. Clause 1.4 (non-admission)**

A non-admission clause is acceptable as a general principle. It must not dilute the specific Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-005 and Ironquay mechanics we are adding.

Add wording that 1.4 does not limit any indemnity, condition or Completion obligation.

**10. Clause 8.3 (buyer knowledge)**

This bars any claim for matters "the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge" of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". That is a blanket actual-and-constructive buyer-knowledge exclusion. It would wipe out most of the warranty package, because we have reviewed the data room.

**Delete 8.3.** If the Seller wants a knowledge qualifier, it should apply to the Seller's warranties only. It should be limited to named Seller knowledge persons, backed by a reasonable-enquiry obligation. It should never excuse Title, Capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Completion-critical items

**11. Bluefen (Clauses 3 / 6.3; DL 2)**

Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and its contract has a change-control consent at clause 11.2 with conditions at clause 11.3. The Seller offers only reasonable endeavours, with the condition "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent. Its own DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

"Addressed" in the Update is therefore not accurate. Delivering a consent letter that is itself conditional would satisfy the Seller's drafting without protecting us.

Pushback:
- Make it a Condition Precedent that requires an effective, unconditional consent (or one whose conditions are all satisfied).
- Require documentary evidence of satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions before Completion.
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. Require at least all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, plus a Buyer-only right to waive the condition.

**12. Riverlark (Clauses 2 / 7; DL 3)**

About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with a change-control at clause 8.1 and discharge at clause 9.2. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in hand.

Under our playbook, a post-completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. We have neither.

Pushback: require all of the following as Completion deliverables:
- a current payout letter (daily interest figure, valid at Completion);
- direct repayment of the facility from Completion funds, deducted as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free price;
- executed deeds of release and discharge of all security, effective on receipt of the payout;
- PPSR and other register discharge steps.

Also check whether the change-control at clause 8.1 is triggered at signing or exchange, not only at Completion.

**13. DD-005 bonuses (funds flow; DL 5)**

AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses sits outside the funds flow, labelled "a matter for the Seller". That is the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion, so we would end up bearing them through the Company. DL 5 also does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.

Pushback:
- Either show them as a specific funds-flow line, paid through Company payroll at Completion and deducted from the price, or have them expressly Seller-funded.
- In either case, include all triggered on-costs and back this with a specific indemnity.
- Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs and confirm the recipients and conditions.

### D. Specific risk items

**14. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DL 4)**

The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment. DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As DL 4 itself concedes, that is not independent verification of non-payment. Neither of us should assume the figure is right or wrong.

The real risk is IP ownership and title to the Project Materials, not just a payment.

Pushback:
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses from any failure of the Company to own or validly use the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims and the cost of re-development or a licence.
- Preserve the cure route: the Seller (or the Company, at the Seller's cost) pays and verifies all SOW3 fees, with bank evidence, and obtains a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally before Completion.
- The indemnity must sit outside the general cap, basket and time limits under its own regime.

**15. DD-006 export incident (Clause 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)**

The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". DL 6 accurately says that access, scope and notification obligations are unknown. We should not overstate it either. We assume no confirmed breach, no harm, no notification duty and no quantified loss.

The Seller's "not material" view is an unsupported conclusion and should not appear as a warranty qualifier.

Pushback: add covenants requiring the Seller and the Company to:
- preserve all logs and evidence;
- continue and complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed or downloaded);
- give the Buyer regular updates and access;
- make any notification decision properly, including the Notifiable Data Breaches assessment under the Privacy Act, in consultation with the Buyer.

We should also seek a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, without fixing any number now.

**16. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)**

The Seller characterises the three renewals (AUD 330,000 total) as ordinary-course costs. DL 8 says nothing about whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks that they be read together. That points to linked or split contracting.

Our playbook position is to assess them, with no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction.

Pushback:
- Do not accept the Seller's characterisation.
- Request the contracts, approval records, termination rights and accrual treatment.
- Reserve treatment (Debt, working capital, leakage or acceptable ordinary-course item) pending that review.
- Add an interim-period covenant that no further renewals are made without Buyer consent.

**17. Lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)**

The Seller describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction that is not triggered by a share sale. Neither appears to depart from the playbook.

However, these are the Seller's readings. We should independently confirm that DD-007 and DD-009 contain no change-of-control trigger, and that the lease does not deem a share transfer to be an assignment. If our review confirms the Seller's reading, add the lease notice to the Completion steps.

### E. Tax, IP and Title

**18. Tax and IP**

The Seller asserts these are "settled under the general regime above". They are **open**. They should not be folded into the general cap and period, and in particular not through the clause 12.3 override.

Keep them as separate categories in our mark-up. Make no concession now, and do not assume unlimited liability or resolution either way.

**19. Title (DD-012; DL 10)**

The Seller relies on the Company's own share register. DL 10 itself states that this "identifies the source relied on" and does not amount to verification.

Pushback: require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, including:
- the ASIC company extract cross-checked to the register;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
- share certificates (or confirmation none were issued);
- the issue and transfer history, with board minutes;
- the constitution and any shareholder agreement (checking for pre-emption rights or a waiver);
- Seller board authority for the sale.

Back this with the uncapped Fundamental warranty regime in item 6.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright and reinstate the playbook position:**
1. Cap: **25% / AUD 6.0m** (not 20%).
2. De minimis **AUD 5,000**; basket **AUD 50,000 tipping** (not AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible).
3. General claims period **24 months** (not 18).
4. Delete the clause 12.3/13 "applies to all Claims" override. General limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
5. A separate **Fundamental/Title regime**: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. An overriding **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5).
7. Delete general disclosure (DL 1.1 and 1.2). Specific fair disclosure only. No disclosure against Title, Capacity, fraud or indemnities.
8. Delete the clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.

**Completion mechanics (Conditions Precedent and deliverables):**

9. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Condition Precedent waivable only by the Buyer. A stronger endeavours standard.
10. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and executed security releases at Completion. Do not accept a post-Completion release.
11. **DD-005 bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs either as a funds-flow line or Seller-funded, with an indemnity.

**Specific protections:**

12. **Ironquay:** a broadened IP indemnity, with the SOW3 cure (verified payment and confirmatory assignment) preserved.
13. **DD-006:** investigation, log-preservation and update covenants, plus a specific indemnity. No assumption of breach or loss.
14. **Sandbar:** request documents and reserve treatment. Add an interim covenant on further renewals.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** independently confirm there is no change-of-control trigger.
16. **Tax and IP:** mark as open and keep in separate categories.
17. **Title:** independent verification deliverables beyond DD-012.

**Internal / process:**

18. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement exists. No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) may be used without her written authority identifying the draft.
19. In our cover note, use the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (items 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10) to show that its Update overstates Bluefen, Riverlark and Title as "addressed".
20. Require a refreshed data-room index and a bring-down of disclosures, because the 22 September cut-off is now stale.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list for the Seller.

"Addressed" in the Update is therefore not accurate. Delivering a consent letter that is itself conditional would satisfy the Seller's drafting without protecting us.

Pushback:
- Make it a Condition Precedent that requires an effective, unconditional consent (or one whose conditions are all satisfied).
- Require documentary evidence of satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions before Completion.
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. Require at least all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours, plus a Buyer-only right to waive the condition.

**12. Riverlark (Clauses 2 / 7; DL 3)**

About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with a change-control at clause 8.1 and discharge at clause 9.2. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in hand.

Under our playbook, a post-completion release needs both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. We have neither.

Pushback: require all of the following as Completion deliverables:
- a current payout letter (daily interest figure, valid at Completion);
- direct repayment of the facility from Completion funds, deducted as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free price;
- executed deeds of release and discharge of all security, effective on receipt of the payout;
- PPSR and other register discharge steps.

Also check whether the change-control at clause 8.1 is triggered at signing or exchange, not only at Completion.

**13. DD-005 bonuses (funds flow; DL 5)**

AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses sits outside the funds flow, labelled "a matter for the Seller". That is the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion, so we would end up bearing them through the Company. DL 5 also does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.

Pushback:
- Either show them as a specific funds-flow line, paid through Company payroll at Completion and deducted from the price, or have them expressly Seller-funded.
- In either case, include all triggered on-costs and back this with a specific indemnity.
- Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs and confirm the recipients and conditions.

### D. Specific risk items

**14. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DL 4)**

The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment. DD-004 clause 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As DL 4 itself concedes, that is not independent verification of non-payment. Neither of us should assume the figure is right or wrong.

The real risk is IP ownership and title to the Project Materials, not just a payment.

Pushback:
- Broaden the indemnity to cover losses from any failure of the Company to own or validly use the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims and the cost of re-development or a licence.
- Preserve the cure route: the Seller (or the Company, at the Seller's cost) pays and verifies all SOW3 fees, with bank evidence, and obtains a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally before Completion.
- The indemnity must sit outside the general cap, basket and time limits under its own regime.

**15. DD-006 export incident (Clause 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)**

The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". DL 6 accurately says that access, scope and notification obligations are unknown. We should not overstate it either. We assume no confirmed breach, no harm, no notification duty and no quantified loss.

The Seller's "not material" view is an unsupported conclusion and should not appear as a warranty qualifier.

Pushback: add covenants requiring the Seller and the Company to:
- preserve all logs and evidence;
- continue and complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed or downloaded);
- give the Buyer regular updates and access;
- make any notification decision properly, including the Notifiable Data Breaches assessment under the Privacy Act, in consultation with the Buyer.

We should also seek a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, without fixing any number now.

**16. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)**

The Seller characterises the three renewals (AUD 330,000 total) as ordinary-course costs. DL 8 says nothing about whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks that they be read together. That points to linked or split contracting.

Our playbook position is to assess them, with no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction.

Pushback:
- Do not accept the Seller's characterisation.
- Request the contracts, approval records, termination rights and accrual treatment.
- Reserve treatment (Debt, working capital, leakage or acceptable ordinary-course item) pending that review.
- Add an interim-period covenant that no further renewals are made without Buyer consent.

**17. Lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)**

The Seller describes these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction that is not triggered by a share sale. Neither appears to depart from the playbook.

However, these are the Seller's readings. We should independently confirm that DD-007 and DD-009 contain no change-of-control trigger, and that the lease does not deem a share transfer to be an assignment. If our review confirms the Seller's reading, add the lease notice to the Completion steps.

### E. Tax, IP and Title

**18. Tax and IP**

The Seller asserts these are "settled under the general regime above". They are **open**. They should not be folded into the general cap and period, and in particular not through the clause 12.3 override.

Keep them as separate categories in our mark-up. Make no concession now, and do not assume unlimited liability or resolution either way.

**19. Title (DD-012; DL 10)**

The Seller relies on the Company's own share register. DL 10 itself states that this "identifies the source relied on" and does not amount to verification.

Pushback: require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, including:
- the ASIC company extract cross-checked to the register;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
- share certificates (or confirmation none were issued);
- the issue and transfer history, with board minutes;
- the constitution and any shareholder agreement (checking for pre-emption rights or a waiver);
- Seller board authority for the sale.

Back this with the uncapped Fundamental warranty regime in item 6.
